patients.summary: Healthy software developer and distance runner who joined in 2023. Exertional rhabdomyolysis with AKI after a hot race in August 2024 needing admission, then cholera twice, after Mexico in 2025 (treated in clinic) and after relief work in Bangladesh in 2026 (ED). Fully recovered each time; no chronic problems or medications.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
26M here to set up primary care. Moved his care from a previous practice; no ongoing issues. Works from home as a software developer and trains for distance races, running most days and racing a few marathons and longer events a year. No complaints today.

PMH: none. PSH: none. Meds: none, no supplements beyond electrolyte drinks on long runs. Allergies: NKDA.
Family hx: father with hypertension; mother with hypothyroidism; an uncle on his father's side with type 2 diabetes.
Social: single, lives in Easthampton. Never smoked, no vaping. Alcohol a drink or two a month. No drugs.

ROS negative across systems.

Exam: lean, well-appearing. Vitals reviewed. HEENT normal, no thyromegaly. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender. Extremities without edema. Skin without lesions of concern. Mood and affect normal.

PHQ-2 0.

A/P:
- Adult preventive care. Baseline CMP, CBC, lipids. One-time HIV and hepatitis C screening discussed and accepted.
- Tdap today, no record of a booster in over 10 years; prior records requested.
- Flu and COVID vaccines when available this fall.
- Runs in heat: talked through hydration and stopping if lightheaded.
Return yearly or as needed.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi August, all of your labs came back normal: kidney and liver function, blood counts and cholesterol all look good, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to do until your next physical.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care practice
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Records received by fax from prior primary care office, 14 pages, scanned to chart. Includes childhood immunization record (routine series complete, including MMR, varicella and hepatitis B) and well visits 2018 to 2022 with normal exams. No problem list, no medications, NKDA. Last tetanus booster recorded in 2010.

documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here after work for flu and COVID shots. Screening questions negative, no prior reactions. Flu vaccine left deltoid, COVID right deltoid. VIS given. Waited 15 minutes without issue.

documents.title: Form for race registration
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, a trail ultra I signed up for this summer wants a medical clearance form signed by a doctor. Attached the PDF. Is that something you can do off my physical from September or do I need to come in?

documents.title: RE: Form for race registration
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Signed and uploaded to your documents tab. Your September visit covers it. Good luck, and drink early and often on the hot days.

events.reason: Low urine output after endurance race

conditions.label: Rhabdomyolysis
conditions.note: exertional, after a race in heat

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
27-year-old man, no medical history, presents with very little urine since finishing a long-distance race yesterday afternoon in high heat. Felt weak and lightheaded after crossing the line and it has not really gone away. Urine he has passed is dark. Takes no medications. NKDA. Never smoker, rare alcohol. Family history of hypertension in father, hypothyroidism in mother, diabetes in a paternal uncle.

Triage: BP 92/58, HR 116, T 38.0 C.
Exam: tired-appearing young man. Skin warm and dry, mucous membranes parched. Lungs clear, heart tachycardic and regular, abdomen benign. No focal neuro deficit.

Results: creatinine 2.4, potassium 5.8, BUN 34. CK 38,600. UA dark, dipstick large blood, microscopy 0-2 RBC, consistent with myoglobinuria.

Assessment: exertional rhabdomyolysis with acute kidney injury and hyperkalemia, in the setting of dehydration after endurance exercise in heat.
Plan: 2 L crystalloid bolus given, then continuous IV fluids targeting high urine output. Repeat potassium and CK in the morning. Admit to medicine.

Allergies: NKDA.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Admit 8/21/2024, discharge 8/23/2024.
Diagnoses: exertional rhabdomyolysis; acute kidney injury; hyperkalemia; dehydration.

Course: 27M admitted from the ED the evening after a hot-weather endurance race with oliguria, CK 38,600, creatinine 2.4 and potassium 5.8. Treated with aggressive IV isotonic fluids for two days with good urine output. Potassium normalized with fluids alone. Urine cleared by the second day. Tolerating diet and walking the halls without symptoms.

Discharge labs (8/23): CK 4,900, creatinine 1.2, potassium 4.3.
Allergies: NKDA. Discharge medications: none. Avoid NSAIDs until kidney function is back to normal.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week for repeat CK and BMP. No running or strenuous exercise until CK normal and cleared by PCP. Return for dark urine, low urine output or muscle pain.

documents.title: Post-discharge follow-up call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Discharge summary received today. Called patient. Home since late morning, feels tired but okay, peeing normally and urine light yellow. Drinking plenty. No muscle pain to speak of. Understands no NSAIDs and no running for now. Scheduled with PCP 8/28 with labs at that visit.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after 2-day admission 8/21 to 8/23 at an outside hospital for exertional rhabdomyolysis with AKI after a race in the heat. Discharge summary reviewed: peak CK 38,600, creatinine 2.4, potassium 5.8, treated with IV fluids; discharge CK 4,900, creatinine 1.2.

Today: feels close to normal. Urine normal color and volume. Has not run since the race. No NSAIDs.

Exam: well-appearing, vitals reviewed. Mucous membranes moist. Thighs and calves nontender, strength full. No edema.

A/P: Exertional rhabdomyolysis with AKI, improving.
- CK and BMP today.
- No running until CK is normal; then a graded return over a few weeks.
- Talked about heat, fluid and sodium intake on long efforts, and stopping when he feels off.
- Hold NSAIDs until creatinine back to baseline.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your CK is down to 620 from 4,900 at discharge, and your creatinine is back to 1.0. Heading the right way. Let's repeat both in about two weeks; still no running until then. Walking is fine.

documents.title: RE: Lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Great, thanks. I'll come in for the draw on the 11th.

documents.title: Repeat labs normal
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news: CK 210 and creatinine 0.96, both normal. The rhabdo and the kidney injury have resolved. You can start running again. Begin with short easy runs every other day and build back over 3 to 4 weeks. Avoid racing in serious heat this season, and if your urine turns dark or your output drops after a hard effort, get checked that day.

documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Flu and COVID vaccines given, left and right deltoid. Tolerated both. Last year's COVID shot gave him a sore arm only. Rescheduled physical for November.

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Back to running since mid-September without trouble, now about 30 miles a week, no races until spring. No dark urine or cramping since the August episode. Otherwise well.

Meds none. NKDA. Never smoker, alcohol a couple of drinks a month.
PHQ-2 0.

Exam: fit, well. Vitals reviewed and normal. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen benign. Musculoskeletal normal. Skin normal.

A/P:
- Healthy adult. History of exertional rhabdomyolysis August 2024, resolved; CK and creatinine normal in September. Revisited heat planning for next season's races.
- Flu and COVID done in October. Tdap 2023. Lipids and HIV/HCV screens done last year.
- Labs not needed today. Return in a year.
